issues.description: The problem statement and UML specify getTotalNumberOfStudents() should return an int, but the solution implements getTotalNumberOfStudents() returning a StudentCount object and adds a StudentCount class. The template does not provide a StudentCount type or indicate a non-primitive return. This mismatch between the specification (int) and the solution (StudentCount) is structural: students following the UML will implement/expect an int return type, while the provided solution diverges and introduces a new type not present in the template, causing confusion and preventing straightforward comparison or use of the solution code.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the return type consistent across artifacts. Either (A) update the problem statement and UML to declare getTotalNumberOfStudents() as returning StudentCount and add the StudentCount class to the template repository so students can use it, or (B) modify the solution to have getTotalNumberOfStudents() return an int (e.g., total number) and remove the StudentCount class from the solution. Ensure the template method stub/signature matches the chosen return type.

issues.description: The problem statement's UML and tasks specify getTotalNumberOfStudents() to return an int (the total number of students). The reference solution, however, implements getTotalNumberOfStudents() to return a StudentCount object and introduces a new class StudentCount. This creates a conceptual mismatch: students reading the UML expect an int result and will implement or test against an int, but the solution uses a different type/name (StudentCount). The differing identifier (StudentCount) and return type break the direct mapping between the problem requirement and the solution implementation, creating unnecessary confusion about the expected API.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the API consistent with the problem UML. Either (A) change the solution to have getTotalNumberOfStudents() return an int (e.g. public int getTotalNumberOfStudents() { return numberOfInscribedStudents + numberOfGuestStudents; }) and remove or keep StudentCount only as an internal helper, updating callers to use the int; or (B) if the StudentCount wrapper is intentional, update the problem statement and UML to declare getTotalNumberOfStudents(): StudentCount and document the StudentCount class. Prefer option (A) to align with the current exercise specification and reduce student confusion.
